introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0760 HISTORY 1, ADVANCED LEVEL, JUNE 2023. Multiple choice question paper. Time allowed: one hour 30 minutes (1h 30). Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination. Check that the question booklet is headed 'Advanced Level - 0760 History 1'. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide on which answer is correct and mark only one answer for each question (if more than one answer is marked, the question scores zero; if you change your mind, erase the first mark carefully). Avoid spending too much time on any one question: move on and come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.
incertitudes: Sujet scanné sans couche texte, lu en image (6 pages). La page de garde indique « 0760 HISTORY 1 », « JUNE 2023 », « ADVANCED LEVEL », « MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTION PAPER », une heure trente ; 50 questions, aucune figure, carte ni document. Filigranes et publicités (gcerevision.com, application « kawlo ») ignorés. Aucun point imprimé (toutes les questions comptent à égalité).

Aucun corrigé officiel n'est fourni : toutes les clés sont déduites de l'historiographie usuelle (manuels camerounais d'histoire, programme du GCE) et n'ont pas pu être confrontées à un barème officiel.

Quatorze QCM ont été convertis en questions ouvertes parce que deux options au moins sont défendables, que l'énoncé est discutable ou que le fait ne peut être vérifié ici : 3 (succès du jihad peul en Adamaoua : Modibo Adama, désunion ou infériorité militaire des Kirdi), 6 (réaction britannique à l'annexion allemande de 1884 : Victoria ou Lock Priso, non vérifié), 7 (question EXCEPT où les quatre options sont des griefs réels contre l'administration allemande), 11 (nationalisme au Southern Cameroons dans les années 1950 : négligence britannique, crise de la Région de l'Est, partis, élite), 12 (chute de Mbida en 1958 : l'option B nomme « Ramadier », nom non cohérent avec les acteurs français habituellement cités), 13 (proposition absente de Bamenda mais adoptée à Foumban : texte des propositions de Bamenda indisponible, clé D donnée à titre provisoire), 14 (Foumban 1961 : faiblesse de négociation ou absence d'experts constitutionnels), 15 (crise du KNDP 1963-1965 et rôle de S.T. Muna : clé C donnée à titre provisoire, non vérifiée), 16 (progrès économique du Cameroun oriental : planification quinquennale ou aide française), 22 (problème des premiers missionnaires en Afrique de l'Ouest : manque de fonds ou rivalité avec les marchands), 32 (Tanzanie et chute d'Amin : invasion du Kagera et hostilité entre États, ou abus d'Amin), 38 (Vérone 1822 : option C reprenant « l'absence de Canning », options confuses), 45 (« première reconnaissance officielle » de la guerre froide : discours de Churchill à Fulton non officiel ; doctrine Truman de 1947 premier acte officiel américain), 49 (obstacle principal à la paix israélo-arabe : Jérusalem ou terre).

QCM conservés avec une clé défendable mais moins sûre : 1 (B : l'abandon des sites ancestraux est la migration elle-même, non une conséquence politique), 5 (A : « serious clashes » est excessif mais seule option nommant la rivalité commerciale anglo-allemande), 10 (A travail forcé retenu plutôt que la politique de mise en valeur), 17 (B autosuffisance alimentaire ; A est un moyen), 18 (B ; l'absence d'opposition et la répression sont des traits du régime, non des explications du progrès), 19 (C « soutien de l'ONU » retenu comme seule cause non reconnue ; l'option D « réalisations visibles de Biya » est une affirmation discutable), 20 (A ; l'adhésion à la Francophonie, option B, est probablement antérieure à Biya, non vérifié), 24 (D : Qadiriyya pour Sokoto, Tijaniyya pour Al-Hajj Umar), 30 (A rupture au sein de l'UGCC retenue plutôt que B, le renvoi de Nkrumah), 31 (A ; le franc CFA, option C, est aussi cité comme effet néfaste), 37 (A refus de la pétition de l'Olive Branch en 1775 comme point culminant de l'« absolutisme » de George III ; formulation de manuel, discutable), 39 (C ; préserver la paix, option A, est un résultat plus qu'un but), 50 (C ; la mort de Staline, option B, ne suffit pas).

Faits historiques énoncés avec prudence dans les corrigés, non vérifiables ici faute de source : Q6 (Victoria / baie d'Ambas placée sous protection britannique puis cédée à l'Allemagne dans les années 1880, sans date précise), Q8 (défaite britannique de Nsanakang en septembre 1914 ; chute de Douala septembre 1914, Yaoundé janvier 1916, Mora 1916), Q12 (rôle des autorités françaises dans la chute de Mbida, sans nom ni date précise), Q13 et Q15 (contenu des propositions de Bamenda, rôle de Muna), Q17 (objectifs de l'« Opération Green Revolution » de 1973, rappelés de façon générale), Q20 (adhésion au Commonwealth en 1995, rétablissement des relations avec Israël en 1986). Aucune statistique ni citation inventée.

Écarts typographiques ou de formulation du sujet imprimé, recopiés avec de légers ajustements : Q6 option C « Hictory Town » lu pour « Hickory Town » ; Q26 option D « Melelik » lu pour « Menelik » ; Q27 « unsuccesful » corrigé en « unsuccessful » ; Q50 option A « Moa Tse-tung » imprimé pour « Mao Tse-tung » (écrit Mao Tse-tung) ; Q37 option B « Williams Pitt » conservé tel qu'imprimé ; Q4 option D (« British crusade to establish the slave trade ») conservée telle qu'imprimée bien qu'historiquement absurde ; La numérotation 44 est suivie de deux points (« 44. . ») sans incidence.

Un seul fichier : Paper 1, un exercice de 50 questions, aucune section, aucune règle de choix (toutes les questions sont obligatoires). Convention des corrigés : les clés ne sont pas confrontées à une clé officielle, donc toute option notée « Intended answer » dans une question ouverte reste une réponse visée, pas une certitude.
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 3, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 22, 32, 38, 45, 49.

Seconde passe faite page par page : énoncés et options relus un à un contre le scan (écarts d'écriture du sujet imprimé : Q13 « Foumban Conference » sans « Constitutional », Q14 « Southern Cameroons politicians », Q32 « Idi Amin Dada », Q6 « Hictory Town », Q26 « Melelik », Q27 « unsuccesful », Q50 « Moa Tse-tung », Q44 option B terminée par « .. »), puis chaque question refaite indépendamment ; aucune clé n'a changé. Faits cités dans les corrigés rédigés avec prudence (voir ci-dessus) ; aucune statistique ni citation inventée.

questions.enonce_markdown: The 19th century pre-colonial ethnic migrations in Cameroon resulted in the following political consequences EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the 19th century several groups moved across the territory of present-day Cameroon, pushed by wars, by the Fulani advance and by the search for land (for example the Chamba who became the Bali, and groups moving into the Grassfields). The arrival of new groups among settled ones led to more wars between ethnic groups (A), to unrest and insecurity (C) and, as migrants and hosts merged under new rulers, to composite kingdoms made of several peoples (D). The abandonment of ancestral sites is not a political consequence of the migrations: it is the migration itself, the movement from which the political changes followed. **Answer: B.**
themes: pre-colonial peoples and states of cameroon

choix.texte: the intensification of inter-ethnic wars.
the abandonment of ancestral sites.
increase in unrest and insecurity.
the birth of composite kingdoms.

questions.enonce_markdown: The centralised states in the Bamenda Grassfields of pre-colonial Cameroon that were different from the others due to their matrilineal systems of inheritance and succession were:
questions.corrige_markdown: Most Grassfields chiefdoms, such as Bafut, Nso and Bali, followed the father's line (patrilineal succession and inheritance). Kom and Aghem were the well-known exceptions: succession and inheritance passed through the mother's line, that is, matrilineal descent. Options A, B and D each include a patrilineal chiefdom (Bafut, Nso or Bali). **Answer: C.**
themes: pre-colonial peoples and states of cameroon

choix.texte: Bafut and Aghem.
Nso and Bali.
Kom and Aghem.
Bali and Kom.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A major reason that accounted for the success of the Fulani Jihads in North Cameroon in the 19th century was:

*Options as printed:* A) the lack of unity among the Kirdi.   B) the efficient leadership of Modibo Adama.   C) the military inferiority of the Kirdi.   D) external support to the Fulani.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The jihad in the Adamawa region was led by Modibo Adama, who received his flag from Usman dan Fodio of Sokoto and organised the conquered lands into lamidates under his authority. His organising ability and his command of a cavalry army are the reason most often given for the success of the jihad. The Kirdi (the non-Muslim peoples of the mountains and plains) lived in small, scattered communities without a common leadership, and this lack of unity and their weaker cavalry also helped the Fulani. No outside army supported the Fulani (D is wrong). Because A and C are also accepted explanations, the choice of the most important one is a matter of emphasis.

**Intended answer: B (the efficient leadership of Modibo Adama).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most appropriate reason for the coming of the Christian missionaries to Cameroon was:
questions.corrige_markdown: The missionaries, beginning with the Baptists on the coast in the 19th century, came above all to preach the Gospel and win converts. Schools, health care and craft training were means to that end, not the main reason (A). They were not agents of annexation (C), and Britain had abolished the slave trade, so a crusade to establish it (D) is false. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: to introduce Western-type education in Cameroon.
to carry out evangelisation among the people of Cameroon.
to prepare the grounds for British annexation of Cameroon.
to participate in the British crusade to establish the slave trade.

questions.enonce_markdown: The scramble for the annexation of Cameroon could be attributed to:
questions.corrige_markdown: On the Cameroon coast in the early 1880s British and German firms competed for the palm oil and rubber trade with the Duala. This rivalry pushed both governments to look for formal control, and Germany won the race when Gustav Nachtigal signed treaties with the Duala kings in July 1884. French traders were not the cause of the competition (B and D), and the dispute was about trade, not a misunderstanding between officials (C). The word 'clashes' is strong, but option A is the only one that names the British-German commercial rivalry. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: serious clashes between British and German firms at the coast.
European commercial rivalry provoked by the attitude of French traders.
misunderstanding between British and German officials in Cameroon.
French fear of the activities of the German traders at the coast.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An outstanding reaction by the British following the German annexation of Cameroon in 1884 was:

*Options as printed:* A) the annexation of Victoria for Britain.   B) the rejection of the annexation treaty.   C) assistance to Lock Priso of Hickory Town against the Germans.   D) the blockade of the coast of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Britain, which had for years not answered the Duala requests for protection, arrived too late: the consul Edward Hewett reached the coast after the Duala kings had signed with Nachtigal. Britain did not blockade the coast and did not contest the treaty by force (B and D). The British reaction that is usually mentioned is to keep the Ambas Bay area around Victoria, the Baptist mission settlement, under British protection; this area was later ceded to Germany in the 1880s. The key is uncertain because the printed options cannot be checked against a source (the British support for Lock Priso, option C, is also mentioned in some accounts).

**Intended answer: A (the annexation of Victoria for Britain).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Antagonism between Cameroonian ethnic groups and the German administration was influenced by the following factors EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) the contempt of the customs and traditions of the people.   B) the violation of middleman monopoly in trade.   C) the arrest and the exile of traditional leaders.   D) the imposition of forced labour.
questions.corrige_markdown:
All four options are recognised causes of conflict between Cameroonians and the German administration: the disregard for local customs (A), the attack on the Duala middleman position when the Germans dealt directly with inland producers (B), the arrest, deportation or execution of chiefs who resisted (C) and forced labour and forced portering on plantations and roads (D). No option can be singled out as the exception.

**No single option can be marked as the exception: the key cannot be established.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major battle fought during World War I in Cameroon whose impact necessitated the creation of the West African Expeditionary Force was:
questions.corrige_markdown: At Nsanakang, on the Cross River frontier of the Southern Cameroons, a small British force was defeated by the Germans in September 1914. The defeat showed that the forces first sent from Nigeria were too few, and Britain and France then built up larger Allied forces for the Cameroon campaign. Douala fell in September 1914 without such a setback, Mora held out until 1916, and Yaounde was taken in January 1916, near the end of the campaign. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the Battle of Mora.
the Battle of Nsanakang.
the Battle of Yaounde.
the Battle of Douala.

questions.enonce_markdown: British neglect of the economy of Southern Cameroons could best be explained by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Britain administered the Southern Cameroons as part of Nigeria (the Eastern Region). The territory had no budget of its own: it depended on funds allocated through Nigeria, and these were small. This administrative arrangement is the best explanation of the neglect. The Nigerian presence (A) was a result, not the cause, and the Mandate did not forbid development (C). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: infiltration of Southern Cameroons by Nigerians.
lack of separate budgetary provision for the territory.
fear not to abrogate the provision of the Mandate.
French determination to unify the two Cameroons.

questions.enonce_markdown: An outstanding economic grievance of French Cameroonians against French rule during the Mandate period was:
questions.corrige_markdown: Under the French Mandate the economic programme (mise en valeur), including the Douala-Yaounde railway, roads and plantations, relied on the compulsory labour of the population, which was the most resented burden. Mise-en-valeur (B) was the French policy of developing the territory, and forced labour was the form in which it hurt people. Option C is a security matter and D a general judgement. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: forced labour.
the policy of Mise-en-valeur.
the activities of Senegalese troops in Douala.
the slow pace of socio-economic growth.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The upsurge of nationalist activities in British Southern Cameroons in the 1950s was largely influenced by:

*Options as printed:* A) the formation of political parties.   B) the Eastern Regional Crisis.   C) British neglect of Southern Cameroons.   D) the activities of the elite.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Southern Cameroons was administered as a part of Nigeria's Eastern Region and received little development, which created a feeling of neglect and domination by Nigerians. The political parties (A) and the educated elite (D) gave this feeling an organised form, and the Eastern Regional crisis of 1953 (B) was one occasion that led to separation from the Eastern Region in 1954. The underlying cause was the neglect.

**Intended answer: C (British neglect of Southern Cameroons).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The fall of Andre-Marie Mbida from power in 1958 was attributed to France in that:

*Options as printed:* A) Mbida was unable to end UPC violent activities.   B) Ramadier masterminded the resignation of his ministers.   C) Mbida's government threatened the unity of French Cameroon.   D) the reunification of French Cameroon was not his priority.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mbida, Prime Minister since 1957, lost office in February 1958 after several of his ministers resigned and his majority collapsed, and Ahmadou Ahidjo became head of government. The French authorities are generally held to have encouraged this change because Mbida had become an obstacle to their plans for the territory. Option B points to that French role, but names Ramadier, which does not match the French officials usually cited in Cameroon (the High Commissioner), so the printed key cannot be confirmed. The other options describe reproaches made at the time but not a French action.

**Intended answer: B (Ramadier masterminded the resignation of his ministers).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A proposal not discussed at the Bamenda All Party Conference but eventually adopted at the Foumban Conference was:

*Options as printed:* A) the proposal for the seat of the Federal Government.   B) the decision on the legal system to adopt.   C) the issue of the currency to use in the Federation.   D) the nature of higher education in both states.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Bamenda All Party Conference (June 1961) fixed the common position of the Southern Cameroons delegation, and the Foumban Constitutional Conference (July 1961) discussed it with President Ahidjo's side and led to the federal Constitution. The question asks for a matter that was not in the Bamenda proposals but ended up in the Foumban texts. The text of the Bamenda proposals is not available here, so the key could not be checked: the seat of the government, the legal system and the currency are matters that were certainly raised in the discussions, and option D is the one retained as the least likely to have been prepared beforehand.

**Intended answer: D (the nature of higher education in both states).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The inability of the Southern Cameroons politicians to defend their aspirations at the Foumban Constitutional Conference of 1961 was largely because of:

*Options as printed:* A) weak bargaining power.   B) failure to make use of constitutional experts.   C) poor knowledge of the French language.   D) fanfare and merry making during the conference.
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the plebiscite of February 1961 the Southern Cameroons had chosen to join the Republic of Cameroon and had no alternative; its delegation went to Foumban without a firm common position and facing a government that had already prepared a draft. That weak bargaining position is the general explanation. The absence of constitutional experts (B) and the ceremonies of the conference (D) are often mentioned as aggravating factors, and language (C) is a lesser one.

**Intended answer: A (weak bargaining power).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The escalation of the KNDP Crisis of 1963-1965 could be attributed to S.T. Muna in that:

*Options as printed:* A) he raised a cloud over his withdrawal/expulsion from the party.   B) he created a rival party to the KNDP by 1965.   C) he outrightly refused to concede defeat in the 1963 KNDP elections.   D) he accepted financial assistance from the KNDP leadership for his campaign.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The KNDP, the governing party of West Cameroon, was split between 1963 and 1965 by rivalry among its leaders, in which Solomon Tandeng Muna was one of the personalities involved. The exact role attributed to Muna in each of the printed options could not be checked with certainty here. Option C, a refusal to accept an internal electoral defeat, is the one that fits the idea of an escalation of a party quarrel, and the other options (a rival party created by 1965, financial help from the leadership) do not match the usual accounts.

**Intended answer: C (he outrightly refused to concede defeat in the 1963 KNDP elections).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Economic progress in the state of East Cameroon could be credited largely to:

*Options as printed:* A) the economic wealth of the territory.   B) the contributions of the French government.   C) the vision and hardwork of East Cameroonians.   D) the introduction of the five-years planning system.
questions.corrige_markdown:
After independence and during the federation the government of East Cameroon organised development through successive five-year plans, which fixed priorities for roads, the railway, agriculture and education. This planning is the feature most often credited with the progress. French aid (B) and the natural wealth of the territory (A) were also important and are the other defensible answers.

**Intended answer: D (the introduction of the five-years planning system).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Recognising agriculture as the backbone of the economy of Cameroon, President Ahidjo launched the 'Operation Green Revolution' in 1973 with the main objective of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Green Revolution of the early 1970s aimed to raise agricultural production so that the country could feed itself and reduce dependence on imported food. Encouraging people, above all the young, to take up farming (A) and providing jobs (C) were means or by-products of that aim, and combating dumping (D) was not its purpose. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: attracting the interest of Cameroonians in agriculture.
ensuring food-sufficiency in Cameroon.
creating jobs for Cameroonians.
checking dumping in Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: Progress and stability under the Ahidjo administration between 1972 and 1982 could best be explained by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Between the creation of the unitary state in 1972 and Ahidjo's resignation in 1982 the government pursued development plans, with investments in infrastructure, schools and health, and this attention to the needs of the population is the best explanation of the progress and stability. The weakness of open opposition (A) and the use of repression (C) were features of the single-party regime but do not explain progress, and natural resources (D) are a condition rather than a policy. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the absence of internal opposition to his government.
measures adopted to provide economic and social satisfaction to Cameroonians.
the excessive use of repressive methods in administration.
the availability of huge natural potentials.

questions.enonce_markdown: Responsibility for the inability of opposition parties to rise to power in Cameroon since 1990 rest on the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: Multiparty politics returned in 1990. The usual explanations of the opposition's failure are the advantages of the party in power (control of the administration, the media and resources), the division of the opposition into many parties and leaders who could not agree on common candidates, and the popularity the government draws from its achievements as presented by its supporters. The United Nations does not support parties in national elections and is not a factor in the opposition's failure, so the exception is C. The printed option D is a debatable claim, which is mentioned in the uncertainties. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the advantages of incumbency.
disunity among the opposition leaders.
lack of support from the UNO.
Biya's visible achievements.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were innovations in Cameroon's foreign policy under President Paul Biya EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: Under Biya Cameroon joined the Commonwealth (1995) and restored diplomatic relations with Israel (1986), which are real innovations in relation to Ahidjo's policy. Close ties with France, on the other hand, were a constant of Cameroon's foreign policy since independence, so upholding them was continuity and not an innovation. The Francophonie option (B) is less clear-cut because Cameroon belonged to the francophone organisations before the 1980s, but A is the best exception. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: upholding special ties with France.
securing membership of Cameroon in La Francophonie.
gaining membership into the Commonwealth of Nations.
re-establishment of ties with Israel.

questions.enonce_markdown: West African chiefs opposed the abolition of the slave trade mainly because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Many coastal and inland rulers earned their revenue from selling captives and from taxes on the trade, and from the goods obtained in exchange. Abolition therefore meant a loss of income, and Britain had to encourage 'legitimate' trade in other products to replace it. The other options are not the reason given in the historical record. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the trade facilitated the process of eliminating criminals within their empires.
the trade was a principal source of income in their communities.
the trade provided wealth to their ancestral heritage.
the trade had destroyed all other economic activities in their kingdoms.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One major problem faced by the early Christian missionaries in West Africa was:

*Options as printed:* A) the rivalry with European traders along the coast.   B) the conflict with the abolitionists over the slave trade.   C) insufficient funding to enhance evangelisation.   D) clashes with consular officials over administration.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The early missions in West Africa depended on the gifts of societies in Europe, and the lack of money and personnel limited the number of stations and schools they could keep. The missionaries were themselves opponents of the slave trade, so a conflict with abolitionists (B) is false. Rivalry with traders (A) was also met in some places and is a defensible alternative.

**Intended answer: C (insufficient funding to enhance evangelisation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were economic motives for the 19th century Jihads in the Western Sudan EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: The jihads had religious, political and economic causes. The need for grazing land for the herds (A), the burden of the taxes laid on the Fulani and their cattle by the Hausa rulers (B) and the wish of the settled Fulani to protect their trade and property (C) are economic motives. The ambition to end oppressive rule (D) is a political and religious motive, not an economic one. The words 'pagan kings' are those of the question. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the Fulani quest for more pastoral land.
opposition to heavy taxation imposed by pagan kings.
the desire of the town Fulani to preserve their wealth.
Fulani ambition to end the oppressive rule of pagan kings.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were similarities between the Sokoto and the Tukolor Islamic Revolutions in West Africa EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: Both revolutions were led by Muslim reformers of Fulani stock (Usman dan Fodio in Hausaland from 1804, Al-Hajj Umar in the western Sudan in the mid-19th century), both drew inspiration from the ideal of a purified and just Islamic state, and both took place in the West African savanna. They differed in the religious brotherhood they followed: Usman dan Fodio belonged to the Qadiriyya, while Al-Hajj Umar was the leader of the Tijaniyya. So the brotherhood doctrines were not common. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: common ethnic solidarity.
common source of inspiration.
common geographical considerations.
common brotherhood doctrines.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Berlin Act of 1885 that marked the end of the Berlin West Africa Conference had the following as major resolutions EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Berlin Act laid down rules for the competition for Africa: free trade in the Congo and Niger basins, notification to the other powers of any new occupation on the coast (D), the principle that occupation must be effective (B), and a statement against the slave trade (C). It did not partition Africa: the actual division was made later by bilateral agreements between the powers. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the partition of the African continent.
the effective occupation of African territories.
the suppression of slave trade in Africa.
notification among European colonial powers.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most immediate factor for the Italo-Abyssinian War of 1895-96 was:
questions.corrige_markdown: By the Treaty of Uccialli (1889) the Italian text made Ethiopia a protectorate of Italy, while the Amharic text did not. When Menelik discovered the difference he rejected the treaty in 1893, and Italy chose war to impose it, which ended in the Italian defeat at Adwa in 1896. Italian economic ambitions (B) and the succession question (C and D) were background factors, while the rejection of the treaty was the immediate cause. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Emperor Menelik's rejection of the Treaty of Uccialli.
Italian socio-economic interest over Abyssinia.
the conflict between Menelik and Mangasha over succession.
Italian opposition to Menelik's succession of Emperor Yahannes.

questions.enonce_markdown: Indirect Rule was unsuccessful in Southern Nigeria due to the fact that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Indirect Rule worked where the British could rule through strong chiefs, as in Northern Nigeria. In many parts of the south, above all among the Igbo, authority was spread among elders and village councils and chiefs had little power, so the British had to create 'warrant chiefs' who were not respected. Option B is too strong, because rulers such as the Yoruba obas and the Oba of Benin existed, and A and D are false. Hence the best answer is C. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the southerners were too uneducated to run the administration.
chieftaincy institutions did not exist in Southern Nigeria.
the chieftaincy institutions were less organised and not influential.
the chieftaincy institutions were too powerful for the British.

questions.enonce_markdown: A distinction between the British Policy of Indirect Rule and the French Policy of Assimilation was that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Indirect Rule kept African rulers and institutions in place under British supervision and so preserved much of the local culture. Assimilation aimed to turn Africans into Frenchmen by teaching them French language and culture, and it treated African institutions as inferior. Option A states a similarity, not a distinction. B oversimplifies, and D is not true, since both policies had failures. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: both policies were European models.
Assimilation was dictatorial while Indirect Rule was liberal.
Indirect Rule safeguarded African culture unlike Assimilation.
Indirect Rule failed where Assimilation was a success.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Second World War influenced the rise of African nationalism in the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: African soldiers who fought for the Allies returned with new ideas and skills and were dissatisfied with colonial rule (B); the United Nations Organisation (C), set up in 1945 on the principle of self-determination, and the Atlantic Charter (D) of 1941, which spoke of the right of peoples to choose their government, encouraged African leaders. The activities of the missionaries began long before the war and are not a consequence of it. **Answer: A.**
themes: impact of world war two on africa

choix.texte: the activities of Christian missionaries.
the return of ex-soldiers.
the creation of the UNO.
the Atlantic Charter Declaration.

questions.enonce_markdown: The formation of the Convention People's Party (CPP) by Nkrumah in 1949 was the consequence of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Kwame Nkrumah was general secretary of the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC), whose leaders were mostly lawyers and businessmen who wanted constitutional change step by step. Nkrumah demanded 'self-government now' and relied on the masses, and the disagreement over this approach, which came to a head around the Coussey Committee in 1949, broke the UGCC and led him to form the CPP in June 1949. Option B names a step in that quarrel but not its cause, and C and D do not match the facts. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the split within the UGCC leadership.
Nkrumah's dismissal from the UGCC.
the UGCC's rejection of the Coussey Constitution.
the lack of an elitist class within the UGCC.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main adverse economic impact of Neo-colonialism in former French Equatorial Africa was:
questions.corrige_markdown: After independence France kept strong economic ties with its former colonies, which continued to export raw materials and import French manufactured goods on terms that favoured France. This unequal trade is the main adverse economic effect. More French investment (B) is not adverse in itself, the CFA franc (C) is a monetary arrangement whose effects are debated, and brain drain (D) is a social matter. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: imbalance in trading activities in favour of France.
an increase in French investments.
the use of the CFA Franc as legal tender.
brain drain from Equatorial Africa.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Tanzanian involvement in the overthrow of Idi Amin Dada in 1979 was the result of:

*Options as printed:* A) the excessive abuse of power within Uganda by Amin.   B) the economic war waged against Asians by Amin.   C) the hostile treatment manifested towards Israel.   D) the hostile external relations with Uganda.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Relations between Amin's Uganda and Julius Nyerere's Tanzania were hostile for years, because Tanzania sheltered Amin's opponents such as Milton Obote. In October 1978 Ugandan troops invaded the Kagera area of Tanzania, and Tanzania counter-attacked and, with Ugandan exiles, took Kampala in April 1979. The immediate cause of the Tanzanian involvement was therefore the hostility and the border war between the two states (D). Amin's abuses at home (A) gave the intervention moral support but were not its cause.

**Intended answer: D (the hostile external relations with Uganda).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major political event that made the date February 11th 1990 a landmark in the history of Apartheid in South Africa was:
questions.corrige_markdown: On 11 February 1990 Nelson Mandela was freed from prison after 27 years, a few days after President de Klerk had lifted the ban on the ANC. The white minority regime did not collapse on that day (A), Apartheid laws were being dismantled and not strengthened (B), and Mandela became president only after the elections of April 1994 (D). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the collapse of the white minority regime.
the strengthening of Apartheid laws.
the release of Nelson Mandela from imprisonment.
the election of Nelson Mandela as pioneer Black president.

questions.enonce_markdown: The natural factors that have been at the origin of refugee problems in Africa are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Refugee problems in Africa have natural and human causes. Prolonged droughts, floods and the resulting famine are natural factors. Oppression, dictatorship, civil wars, political upheavals, insecurity and coups are all man-made. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: prolonged droughts, floods and famine.
oppression and dictatorship.
civil wars and political upheavals.
insecurity and military coups.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Rwandan Civil War of 1994 was:
questions.corrige_markdown: The war between the Hutu-led government and the Rwandan Patriotic Front, largely made up of Tutsi exiles, and the genocide of Tutsi and moderate Hutu in 1994 were fought along the ethnic division between Hutu and Tutsi that colonial rule had hardened. It was therefore an inter-ethnic conflict. It was not a struggle against colonial rule (D), and the farmer-herder explanation (B) is a simplification of that ethnic division. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: an inter-community violence.
a farmer-herder conflict.
an inter-ethnic conflict.
an anti-colonial struggle.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important legislation passed after the 1688 English Revolution that guaranteed the supremacy of Parliament over the Crown was:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Bill of Rights of 1689 was the main law that settled the relation between Crown and Parliament after the overthrow of James II: the king could not suspend laws, raise taxes or keep an army in peacetime without Parliament's consent, and elections and debates were to be free. The Mutiny Act, the Triennial Act and the Septennial Act dealt with the army and the length of parliaments, which were more limited matters. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the Bill of Rights of 1689.
the Mutiny Act of 1689.
the Septennial Act of 1716.
the Triennial Act of 1694.

questions.enonce_markdown: The absolutism of King George III attained its climax when:
questions.corrige_markdown: In July 1775 the Second Continental Congress sent the Olive Branch Petition, which asked the king to stop the conflict and take the colonists' complaints into account. George III refused to receive it and declared the colonies to be in rebellion, which closed the way to reconciliation and is generally shown as the high point of his uncompromising attitude. The dismissal of ministers (B), the Quebec Act (C) and the old mercantilist rules (D) belong to earlier or more general steps. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: he outrightly rejected the Olive Branch Petition from the Colonists.
he dismissed Williams Pitt and George Grenville as ministers.
he forced Parliament to pass the Quebec Act in 1774.
he enforced the old colonial policy of Mercantilism.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A significant setback to the objectives of the Congress Powers at Verona was:

*Options as printed:* A) French intervention in the revolution in Spain.   B) the declaration of the Monroe Doctrine by America.   C) the absence of the British Foreign Secretary, George Canning.   D) the disagreement among the Protocol Powers.
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the Congress of Verona (1822) Austria, Russia and Prussia wanted joint action against the revolutions, but Britain refused to support intervention in Spain, and under Canning British policy turned away from the Congress system. The French intervention in Spain (A) was an aim the congress approved, not a setback. The Monroe Doctrine (B) came in 1823, after Verona. The printed options are confused (Canning was not Foreign Secretary at the time of the congress, and the 'Protocol Powers' are not defined).

**Intended answer: C (the absence of the British Foreign Secretary, George Canning).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The system of Alliances put in place by Bismarck was aimed principally at:
questions.corrige_markdown: After defeating France in 1871 and annexing Alsace-Lorraine, Bismarck expected French revenge and built his alliances (the Three Emperors' League, the Dual Alliance, the Triple Alliance, the Reinsurance Treaty) to keep France without allies and so to protect Germany. Peace was the result he wanted (A), but the principal aim was security against France. Isolating Austria and Russia (B) is the opposite of his policy of keeping them close. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: preserving the peace of Europe.
isolating both Austria and Russia.
securing Germany against France.
keeping Italy neutral in Europe.

questions.enonce_markdown: The outbreak of war in Europe in 1914 and its subsequent transformation into a global war was mainly due to:
questions.corrige_markdown: A quarrel between Austria-Hungary and Serbia became a war of the great powers because the two blocs, the Triple Alliance and the Triple Entente, drew in their members one after another, and the empires' colonies and allies then widened it into a world war. The alliance system as a whole is the answer, because A and C each describe only one of the two blocs. The attack on Belgium (D) brought Britain in but followed from the German war plan. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the Triple Alliance.
the existence of the Alliance System.
the Triple Entente.
Germany's attack of Belgium.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important principle applied at the Paris Peace Conference of 1919 was:
questions.corrige_markdown: President Wilson's Fourteen Points made self-determination of peoples the guiding principle, and it was used to redraw the map of central and eastern Europe after the fall of the Austro-Hungarian, German, Russian and Ottoman empires, even though it was applied unevenly. Balance of power (B) was the older approach that Wilson rejected. Reparations (D) were imposed on the defeated but are not a principle of peacemaking in the same sense. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the principle of self-determination.
the principle of balance of power.
the principle of nationalism.
the principle of paying reparations.

questions.enonce_markdown: The successes of the League of Nations in the 1920s could be attributed to all the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the 1920s the League settled disputes such as the Aaland Islands and the Greek-Bulgarian incident because the states involved were small (B), because people in Europe still remembered the war and wanted peace (C), and because Germany and Russia, the powers most likely to cause trouble, were disarmed and weak (D). A lack of confidence in the League by the European states would have weakened it and is not a reason for its successes. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the lack of confidence in the association by most European Nations.
most of the conflicts it settled involved smaller and weaker powers.
the scars of war were still fresh in Europe in the 1920s.
major powers like Germany and Russia were disarmed and weak.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important event in the 1930s that symbolised the final collapse of the League of Nations was:
questions.corrige_markdown: The League had failed to stop Japan in Manchuria (1931), Italy in Abyssinia (1935) and Germany's steps against its neighbours. The outbreak of the Second World War in 1939 showed that it had failed in its first purpose, the preservation of peace, and it did nothing during the war. The Nazi-Soviet Pact (A) and the attack on Czechoslovakia (D) were steps before the war, and the Grand Alliance (B) belongs to the war years. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the signing of the Nazi-Soviet Pact.
the formation of the Grand Alliance.
the outbreak of the Second World War.
Hitler's attack of Czechoslovakia.

questions.enonce_markdown: An adverse political effect of the Second World War was:
questions.corrige_markdown: The war left the United States and the Soviet Union as the two superpowers with opposed systems, and their distrust grew into the Cold War, a political effect that shaped international relations for decades. The refugees (A) and the destruction of the Jews (B) are social and humanitarian effects, and the loss of purchasing power (D) is economic. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the high number of refugees in the world.
the mass elimination of Jews in Europe.
the escalation of the East-West tension.
the decline in purchasing power in Europe.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The first official recognition of the existence of the Cold War was in:

*Options as printed:* A) the Iron Curtain Speech of Winston Churchill.   B) President Truman's outburst on the Soviet Union at Potsdam.   C) the unwillingness of Britain and France to ally with Russia in 1938.   D) the disagreement among the Allies at Yalta in 1945.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The speech given by Winston Churchill at Fulton, Missouri, in March 1946, in which he said that an iron curtain had descended across Europe, is the event usually quoted as the public recognition of the split between East and West. Churchill was no longer prime minister when he spoke, so the speech was not strictly an 'official' statement, and the first official American declaration of the policy of containment is the Truman Doctrine of 1947.

**Intended answer: A (the Iron Curtain Speech of Winston Churchill).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Korea became a Cold War theatre in the early 1950s mainly because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Korea had been divided at the 38th parallel after 1945 between a Soviet-backed North and an American-backed South. When North Korea invaded the South in 1950, the United States led a UN force to defend the South, because its policy of containment was to stop communism from spreading, and China later entered the war. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the Japanese wanted to regain their colony.
both Koreas wanted an end to foreign occupation.
the UNO wanted to challenge Communist Russia.
the USA wanted to contain the spread of Communism.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most outstanding factor that blocked decision making at the UN Security Council has been:
questions.corrige_markdown: Each of the five permanent members (the USA, the USSR or Russia, Britain, France and China) can block any substantive resolution by a veto. During the Cold War and since, the use of the veto to protect national interests has often paralysed the Council. The Council has only fifteen members, of whom five are permanent, and the Secretary General has no power to decide for it. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the lack of interest among Security Council members.
the membership of many smaller states in the Council.
the abuse in the use of veto powers by the permanent members.
the dictatorship of the UN Secretary Generals.

questions.enonce_markdown: Among the objectives of La Francophonie the most significant for France is:
questions.corrige_markdown: For France La Francophonie is first of all a means of defending and spreading the French language and, with it, French culture and influence in the world, above all among its former colonies. The other aims it declares, such as democracy, the rights of states and cooperation in communication technologies, are shared objectives of the member countries. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the promotion of the French language as an international language.
the promotion of democratic practices among member countries.
the support for the rights and independence of member states.
the promotion of new technologies of communication.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The main obstacle towards a lasting peace settlement of the protracted Arab-Israeli Crisis in the Middle East is:

*Options as printed:* A) the problem of land ownership.   B) the conflict over ownership of Jerusalem.   C) the presence of oil deposits.   D) Western powers' support to Israel.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The status of Jerusalem, a holy city for Jews, Muslims and Christians that both Israelis and Palestinians claim as their capital, is the point on which negotiations have repeatedly failed. Territory and the Palestinian refugees (A) are also major obstacles and are the other defensible answer. Oil (C) and Western support (D) are background factors.

**Intended answer: B (the conflict over ownership of Jerusalem).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Sino-Soviet friendship was so short-lived mainly because:
questions.corrige_markdown: China and the Soviet Union signed a treaty of friendship and alliance in 1950, but the Soviet leaders expected to lead the Communist bloc, while the Chinese leaders, who had won their own revolution, refused to be subordinate. This quarrel over leadership, together with disagreements about doctrine after Stalin's death, brought the break of the late 1950s and the 1960s. Stalin's death alone (B) does not explain it, and the Soviet Union did give aid to China in the 1950s (D). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Stalin did not appreciate Mao Tse-tung's leadership in China.
of the death of Josef Stalin in 1953.
the USSR wanted China to be a satellite of the Communist Bloc.
the Soviet Union provided no assistance to China since 1949.
